title: myDAS: QR Code Document Submission System
image1Description: Automated kiosk station for physical document check-in and tracking via QR Code

section1.heading: Inspiration
section1.content: As part of the Digital Accounting System (DAS) initiative, I identified that the primary bottleneck was the delivery of original physical documents to the accounting department. Previously, there was no clear management system; employees hand-delivered documents without knowing the specific drop-off point or responsible officer. This led to lost documents, untraceable statuses, and delayed accounting entries. I initiated the development of a QR-enabled automated station to create a systematic hub that connects employees to accounting with 100% transparency and auditability.

section2.heading: Concept and Design
section2.content: The system is designed for ease of use via a 'Smart Station.' Employees simply scan a pre-generated QR code from the system at the drop-off point and enter their contact details. The system then updates the document status to 'Submitted' and sends an instant email notification to accounting staff. Additionally, I implemented an Automated Reminder system that alerts employees of pending documents every morning and generates a summary of received items for the accounting intake desk to ensure a continuous workflow.

section3.heading: Challenges and Solutions
section3.content: A major challenge was Physical Terminal Security, as the kiosk is located in a public area. I designed the software to operate in a strict 'Kiosk Mode,' restricting access to a single application window. To prevent unauthorized command inputs, physical keyboards were removed, and the full-screen mode was protected by an admin-level password. This robust design minimizes data security vulnerabilities and prevents external interference with the system's core functions.

section4.heading: Opportunities for Further Development
section4.content: In the future, the system could evolve into 'Autonomous Printing & Submission' to further reduce the manual workload. If an employee receives a secure e-Document, the system could accept the file online and automatically print it at the receiving station, updating the status instantly. This would centralize both paper and digital documents into a single source of truth, maximizing the efficiency of the organization's document lifecycle.
